title: Functions Quiz 3
description: Swap and solve. Check that an inverse exists first.
instructions: Write maths answers with the keypad. Any equal form is accepted.
Every question has a trap. Slow down at the signs.

questions.question: Find $f^{-1}(x)$ for $f(x)=3x-2$.
questions.explanation: Write $y=3x-2$, so $x=\dfrac{y+2}{3}$. Watch out: add $2$ before dividing by $3$.

questions.question: If $f(x)=2x-5$, find $f^{-1}(7)$.
questions.explanation: Solve $2x-5=7$: $x=6$. Watch out: you solve $f(x)=7$, you do not substitute $7$ into $f$.

questions.question: Find $f^{-1}(x)$ for $f(x)=\dfrac{x+1}{x-2}$.
questions.explanation: $y(x-2)=x+1$ gives $x(y-1)=2y+1$, so $x=\dfrac{2y+1}{y-1}$. Watch out: collect the $x$ terms on one side before factoring.

questions.question: Which function has an inverse over all real numbers?
questions.explanation: Only $x^3+1$ is one-to-one on all of $\mathbb R$. Watch out: $x^2$ and $|x|$ give the same output for $x$ and $-x$.

questions.question: $f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac{1}{f(x)}$.
questions.explanation: The inverse undoes $f$; $\dfrac1{f(x)}$ is the reciprocal. For $f(x)=2x$, $f^{-1}(x)=\dfrac x2$ but $\dfrac1{f(x)}=\dfrac1{2x}$. Watch out: the $-1$ is not an exponent here.

questions.question: What is the inverse of $f(x)=e^{x}$?
questions.explanation: Logarithm undoes the exponential. Watch out: $e^{-x}$ is the reciprocal, not the inverse.

questions.question: Find $f^{-1}(x)$ for $f(x)=x^{3}+1$.
questions.explanation: $y=x^3+1$ gives $x=\sqrt[3]{y-1}$. Watch out: subtract $1$ first, then take the cube root.

questions.question: Find $f^{-1}$ for $f(x)=\dfrac{2x}{x+1}$. One step is wrong. Tap it, then choose the correct step.
questions.explanation: $yx-2x=-y$ gives $x(y-2)=-y$. Watch out: moving $y$ across changes its sign.

questions.question: A function must pass the horizontal line test to have an inverse.
questions.explanation: If a horizontal line crosses twice, two inputs share one output and the inverse is not a function. Watch out: this is different from the vertical line test.

questions.question: The point $(2,5)$ is on the graph of $f$. What is $f^{-1}(5)$?
questions.explanation: The inverse swaps coordinates, so $(5,2)$ is on $f^{-1}$. Watch out: swap the coordinates, do not negate.
